subject: On-prem delivery: operator certification timeline & escrow-lite checklist
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi@careco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19 09:06 -0700
Subject: Request: operator certification + escrow-lite for on-prem deployment

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and IT want to lock down a couple items before the PO:
- formal operator certification checklist (controls/operators who will touch on-prem infra)
- an "escrow-lite" path for evidence of operator access if we need to validate in an audit (not full code escrow, just custody and attestation steps)

Can Redwood provide a template checklist and indicate where you will accept redlines in the MSA / Order Form? We need to present an internal timeline to legal by 7/26.

Ravi
Ravi Shah
Head of Infrastructure, CareCo
(itops@careco.com)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@careco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19 11:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator certification + escrow-lite for on-prem deployment

Ravi — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Laura (legal) and Marissa (private deployments) so we can align on redlines and the technical checklist. Attached: a one-page Operator Certification Checklist draft that we use for private customers.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Laura to confirm what MSA/Order Form language is negotiable for an "escrow-lite" attestation and audit window.
2) Marissa to confirm what operator artifacts we can provide (runbook excerpts, access logs, snapshot attestation) and expected delivery lead time.
3) You share any procurement contact / PO timeline and whether CareCo prefers us to accept redlines in the MSA or an annex.

We can target a consolidated response + redline packet by 7/21 EOD so your legal team has time before 7/26.

Attachments: Operator-Certification-Checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@careco.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20 08:52 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator certification + escrow-lite for on-prem deployment

Ravi / team —

Thanks — I reviewed the Operator Certification Checklist and sketched a set of reasonable redlines for the MSA and Order Form. High-level comments below (full redline attached):

- License scope: narrow to runtime and customer's data only; exclude developer/source-level IP from any delivery or escrow obligations.
- Operator access: define a scoped operator role limited to named activities (snapshot/restore, health checks). No blanket "admin" access.
- Audit window & evidence: propose a 90-day audit window for ticketed requests; for on-prem we can provide an attested snapshot plus signed access logs. Add language that remote access is performed only under documented change control and with prior notice.
- Escrow-lite: propose an annexed process rather than adding terms directly to the MSA. Annex would include steps: evidence request → verification call → signed operator attestation → delivery of artifact (snapshot/logs). We will not transfer private keys or full operator credentials; instead we will provide signed attestations.
- SLA/availability carveouts for operator intervention periods (we can enumerate these in the Order Form).

Please find attached a redline of the MSA (Redline_MSA_CareCo_2027-07-20.docx) with suggested language. Key asks for CareCo legal: confirm whether a 90-day audit window and attestation-based evidence is acceptable, and confirm whether you require escrow to be with a third-party steward or if an annexed attestation model is sufficient.

If CareCo insists on a third-party escrow steward who must hold keys, we'll need to escalate (this is not our standard model).

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the redlines — availability below.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ravi Shah <ravi@careco.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-21 07:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator certification + escrow-lite for on-prem deployment

Laura — thanks for the detailed redline. A couple quick clarifying points from procurement/legal: 
- CareCo's standard is a 120-day audit window, but we can consider 90 days if coupled with a documented escalation path.
- We prefer a third-party escrow steward for very high-sensitivity workloads; for this initial rollout (non-PHI) an attestation annex may be acceptable.

Two quick questions: 1) can you confirm what exact artifacts Redwood would deliver (e.g., VM snapshot, signed access logs, runbook excerpt)? 2) who at Redwood will sign the operator attestation (title, name)?

Ravi

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@careco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Everest Legal <procurement@everest.com>
Date: 2027-07-23 16:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator certification + escrow-lite for on-prem deployment

Ravi — appreciate the quick review and flexibility. Consolidated answers and next steps below (so legal/procurement has a single record):

Artifacts Redwood can provide (annexed attestation workflow):
- Signed operator attestation (signed by Head of Platform Operations or delegated program lead)
- Time-bound access logs for operator sessions (syslog export, redacted sensitive fields)
- Minimal runbook excerpts for recovery steps (no source code or internal configs)
- Optional encrypted snapshot (we only provide an attestation to snapshot existence; keys are not handed over)

Signing authority: Head of Platform Operations (currently: Marissa Cole) will be the default signatory for operator attestations. If you need a specific name in the contract, we can list Marissa Cole, Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference.

Audit window: Redwood can accept a 90-day audit window by default; we will accept 120 days for this PO if CareCo commits to an escalation cadence (we propose a 2-week response SLA for scheduling an evidence verification call).

Next steps / timeline:
- 7/23: Redwood posts redlined MSA (attached) and the operator checklist.
- 7/24: CareCo to indicate preferred audit window (90 vs 120) and confirm whether a third-party escrow steward is required.
- 7/26: Target for CareCo legal to circulate counter-redlines / acceptance.
- Upon agreement: DocuSign order form to be sent.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC12345 (OrderForm HC-7032)

Attachments: Redline_MSA_CareCo_2027-07-20.docx; Operator-Certification-Checklist.pdf; DocuSign_OrderForm_HC-7032.pdf

Thanks — I can join a working call on 7/24 09:00–10:00 PT if that helps.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: DocuSign_OrderForm_HC-7032.pdf)
